paragraphs.title: Drowning, Persecution, and Acknowledgment of Guilt

answers: As a journey through the wilderness
As sinking in water and mire
easy.explanation: He says that the waters have come in unto his soul and that he sinks in deep mire.
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe his distress?

answers: They are more numerous than the hairs of his head
They are only members of his family
easy.explanation: He says that those who hate him without a cause are more than the hairs of his head.
easy.q: What does the psalmist say about those who hate him?

easy.explanation: The psalmist says, “Thou knowest my foolishness; and my sins are not hid from thee.”
easy.q: What does God know about the psalmist?

answers: Because he is sinking and being opposed
Because he wants to leave his people
medium.explanation: He is sinking in deep waters and is surrounded by enemies.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask to be saved?

answers: That his distress has reached the depths of his life
That he has found a spring
medium.explanation: The expression describes extreme danger and distress.
medium.q: What does “the waters are come in unto my soul” communicate?

answers: The psalmist describes many enemies while admitting that God knows his sins
The psalmist describes joy and loneliness
The psalmist describes riches and blessing
medium.explanation: He speaks of persecution but also acknowledges his own sins before God.
medium.q: What contrast appears in this passage?

answers: He is in danger and has no firm place to stand
He is preparing for a journey
challenge.explanation: “There is no standing” and the overflowing floods show his helplessness.
challenge.q: What does the image of drowning emphasize about the psalmist’s condition?

answers: He does not claim that everything about him is perfect
challenge.explanation: Although he describes persecution, he admits that God knows his sins.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the psalmist’s acknowledgment of his sins?

answers: As accusations unrelated to the psalmist
challenge.explanation: He calls them enemies who would destroy him wrongfully and says he restored what he did not take.
challenge.q: How are the enemies’ accusations presented?

paragraphs.title: Disgrace, Isolation, and Faithfulness to God

answers: For those who wait on and seek God
easy.explanation: He asks that those who wait on and seek God not be ashamed or confounded for his sake.
easy.q: For whose sake does the psalmist ask that shame not come?

answers: He has become a stranger to his brethren
He has moved in with them
easy.explanation: He says, “I am become a stranger unto my brethren.”
easy.q: How has the psalmist’s family relationship changed?

answers: They speak against him and mock him
easy.explanation: Those sitting in the gate speak against him, and he becomes the song of the drunkards.
easy.q: How does the public respond to him?

answers: His zeal for God’s house and his identification with God
medium.explanation: He says, “The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up,” and that reproaches against God fell upon him.
medium.q: What caused the psalmist’s reproach, according to the passage?

medium.explanation: Reproach refers to the disgrace and insults he suffers.
medium.q: What does “reproach” mean in this passage?

answers: He wept, fasted, and wore sackcloth
He celebrated with the people of the city
medium.explanation: He describes chastening his soul with fasting and making sackcloth his garment.
medium.q: What did the psalmist do during his distress?

answers: He fears that his humiliation may discourage or shame them
challenge.explanation: He asks that those who seek God not be confounded for his sake.
challenge.q: Why does the psalmist mention the possible shame of those who seek God?

answers: His devotion to God is presented as part of the background to his disgrace and isolation
His family praised him for his zeal
challenge.explanation: After mentioning his zeal, he describes becoming a stranger to his family and a mockery to the public.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between zeal for God’s house and family alienation?

answers: He became an object of ridicule
challenge.explanation: His condition became a saying or example used by others to mock him.
challenge.q: What does it mean that the psalmist became “a proverb” to others?

paragraphs.title: A Prayer for Rescue from Water and Enemies

answers: Unto those sitting in the gate
easy.explanation: He directs his prayer to the LORD and asks Him to hear and save him.
easy.q: To whom does the psalmist pray?

answers: From the mire, the waters, and those who hate him
easy.explanation: He asks to be delivered from the mire, deep waters, and his enemies.
easy.q: From what does the psalmist ask to be delivered?

easy.explanation: He asks God to draw nigh unto his soul and redeem it.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask God to do for his soul?

medium.explanation: He says, “My prayer is unto thee, O LORD, in an acceptable time.”
medium.q: At what time does the psalmist ask God to hear him?

answers: He asks not to be swallowed up completely
He asks the pit to fill with water
He asks the pit to light his way
medium.explanation: The image describes being trapped or swallowed by overwhelming danger.
medium.q: What does “let not the pit shut her mouth upon me” suggest?

answers: Because he is in trouble and needs mercy
medium.explanation: He says he is in trouble and asks God to hear him speedily.
medium.q: Why does he ask God to turn unto him?

answers: The imagery becomes a request for rescue from drowning
The imagery becomes a picture of celebration
challenge.explanation: The psalmist again mentions mire, floods, deep waters, and the pit while asking for deliverance.
challenge.q: How does the prayer repeat the water imagery from the beginning?

answers: It emphasizes that his enemies contribute to his danger
It says that his enemies help him
It cancels the request for rescue
challenge.explanation: He asks to be redeemed and delivered because of the opposition of his enemies.
challenge.q: What does “because of mine enemies” add to the request for redemption?

answers: God’s lovingkindness, tender mercies, and salvation
challenge.explanation: He appeals to God’s lovingkindness, mercy, and salvation.
challenge.q: On what does the psalmist base his confidence that God will hear him?

paragraphs.title: Brokenheartedness and a Plea for Justice

easy.explanation: He says, “Reproach hath broken my heart.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist say about his heart?

easy.explanation: He looked for comforters but found none.
easy.q: What did the psalmist fail to find?

answers: That they be judged and not counted with the righteous
easy.explanation: He asks that they be blotted out and not written with the righteous.
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask to happen to his enemies?

medium.explanation: Instead of comfort, they gave him gall for meat and vinegar for drink.
medium.q: What kind of treatment did the psalmist receive?

medium.explanation: Gall and vinegar symbolize bitter and cruel treatment.
medium.q: What does “gall” represent in this passage?

answers: What should have been for their welfare becomes a trap
The table becomes a place of prayer
They invite the poor to eat there
medium.explanation: The psalmist asks that their table and expected welfare become a trap.
medium.q: How does the enemies’ table become a snare?

answers: The lack of comfort deepens his pain and leads him to ask for justice
The absence of comfort makes him joyful
challenge.explanation: After describing his broken heart and lack of pity, he asks God to judge his enemies.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the absence of comforters and the plea for judgment?

answers: A movement from personal distress to a plea for justice
A movement from joy to wealth
A movement from prayer to thanksgiving
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with his pain and continues with requests for judgment.
challenge.q: What does the movement from personal suffering to requests against the enemies show?

answers: They should not be counted among God’s righteous people
They should not learn to read
They should not live in the city
challenge.explanation: The psalmist asks that they not be written with the righteous in the book of the living.
challenge.q: What does the request that the enemies not be written with the righteous mean?

paragraphs.title: Salvation, Thanksgiving, and Encouragement for the Humble

easy.explanation: He says, “I am poor and sorrowful.”
easy.q: How does the psalmist describe himself?

easy.explanation: He will praise God with a song and magnify Him with thanksgiving.
easy.q: How will the psalmist praise God?

answers: The humble and those who seek God
Those sitting in the gate only
easy.explanation: The humble shall see and be glad, and those who seek God shall have living hearts.
easy.q: Who will be glad when God brings salvation?

answers: The humble will see God’s salvation and be glad
medium.explanation: His salvation and praise become a source of joy for the humble and those who seek God.
medium.q: Why will the psalmist’s thanksgiving encourage others?

medium.explanation: The verse compares thanksgiving with an ox or bullock bearing horns and hoofs.
medium.q: What does “a bullock that hath horns and hoofs” describe?

answers: Thanksgiving is presented as pleasing and valuable to God
medium.explanation: The psalmist says that praise and thanksgiving please the LORD better than an ox or bullock.
medium.q: What does the comparison between song, thanksgiving, and sacrifice teach?

answers: It moves from his suffering to the encouragement of the humble
It moves from prayer to wealth
It moves from praise to revenge
challenge.explanation: After describing himself as poor and sorrowful, he emphasizes how salvation will help others.
challenge.q: How does the focus of the passage change from the psalmist’s personal condition?

answers: God hears and values those who suffer and lack power
challenge.explanation: The verse assures the poor and afflicted that God does not reject them.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the statement that the LORD despises not His prisoners?

answers: The psalmist expects salvation to lead to praise
He wants to punish the poor
challenge.explanation: He promises to praise and magnify God in response to His saving work.
challenge.q: Why does thanksgiving appear after the request for salvation?

paragraphs.title: Praise of Creation and the Restoration of Zion and Judah

answers: Heaven, earth, the seas, and everything that moves in them
Those sitting in the gate only
easy.explanation: The psalm calls the whole created order to praise God.
easy.q: Who is called to praise God?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “For God will save Zion.”
easy.q: What will God do for Zion?

easy.explanation: God will build the cities of Judah.
easy.q: What will happen to the cities of Judah?

answers: God’s salvation and rebuilding will allow His servants to dwell there and possess it
Salvation will cause the people to leave
medium.explanation: The rebuilt cities will become a dwelling and possession for God’s servants.
medium.q: What is the connection between saving Zion and the people dwelling there?

medium.explanation: The verse speaks of receiving the land and cities as an inheritance.
medium.q: What does “inherit it” mean in this context?

answers: The seed of God’s servants and those who love His name
Those sitting in the gate only
medium.explanation: The passage names the seed of His servants and those who love His name.
medium.q: Who is promised a dwelling in the restored land?

answers: From individual distress to praise of creation and restoration of the community
challenge.explanation: The ending broadens the focus from the psalmist to creation, Zion, Judah, and God’s people.
challenge.q: What is the central movement in the conclusion of the psalm?

answers: Praise is not limited to one person or group
Only the people of Judah may praise
challenge.explanation: Heaven, earth, the seas, and every moving thing are all summoned to praise.
challenge.q: What does calling all creation to praise God emphasize?

answers: They will dwell in the restored cities
They are not connected with the cities
challenge.explanation: The final verse says that those who love His name shall dwell therein.
challenge.q: How are those who love God’s name connected with the future of Judah’s cities?
